sections.content:
You know *pasar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 23. In economic reporting, *pasar a* + infinitive highlights a clear transition from one stage, rank or role to another—often marking a turning point in trade, production or policy.

It pairs especially often with *ser*, *ocupar*, *representar*, *depender* and *impulsar*: *pasó a ser el principal exportador*, *la exportación pasó a impulsar el crecimiento*. Unlike *empezar a* (which merely marks a beginning), *pasar a* implies a previous state that changed.

sections.title: pasar a + infinitive for market shifts
rows: pasar a ser: El país pasó a ser un gran exportador de energía.
The country went on to become a major energy exporter.
pasar a ocupar: El sector industrial pasó a ocupar el primer lugar.
The industrial sector moved into first place.
pasar a depender de: La economía pasó a depender más de la exportación.
The economy came to depend more on exports.
pasar a impulsar: La demanda externa pasó a impulsar la producción.
External demand took over as the driver of production.

items.spanish: En una década, la región pasó a ser el principal exportador del sector.
items.english: Within a decade, the region went on to become the sector's main exporter.

items.spanish: Al caer el consumo interno, las empresas pasaron a buscar mercados externos.
items.english: When domestic consumption fell, companies shifted to seeking external markets.

items.spanish: Tras la reforma, la producción local pasó a cubrir casi toda la demanda.
items.english: After the reform, local production went on to cover almost all demand.

sections.content: *Pasar a* always requires the preposition *a* before the infinitive (*pasó a ser*, never *pasó ser* or *pasó de ser*). Remember that *pasar de* + infinitive is informal for 'not to bother doing' and does not mean 'to move on to'.
